newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SMALL APOLOGISES FOR "DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOUR".
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SMALL APOLOGISES FOR "DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOUR".

text.p: Natal wing James Small apologised to the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) and the public on Thursday for partying at a nightclub two days before an international against New Zealand.
Small, whose likely return to the Springbok side was made possible by the intervention of SARFU president Louis Luyt on Wednesday, made his peace in a statement.
"I would like to offer my apologies...for any disruption caused by my going out to a nightclub," he said.
Small said he had a good relationship with most of his Springbok team mates.
"Rugby is my life and playing for this country in the green and gold is the greatest honour I have ever had."
Small had been reminded by a SARFU management committee on Wednesday of "what was expected of a professional player of his calibre".

Small, the most capped Springbok in the post-isolation period with 31 appearances, is expected to be named later this month in the South African squad to tour Argentina, France and Wales in November and December.
